_title: How to Get to Hallstatt by Train | WoW Train · glosx.app
_desc: How to reach Hallstatt by train: the station is across the lake and a ferry meets every train to carry you to the village.
b1: How to Get to Hallstatt by Train
b2: By WoW Train · Updated June 2026 · 3 min read
b3: A fairytale village on a glassy alpine lake, ringed by mountains. Hallstatt looks impossible to reach — but the train does it beautifully, and the last step is pure magic: a little ferry that meets you on the water.
b4: What is the route from Salzburg?
b5: The most common way in is from Salzburg. There's no single direct train the whole way — you change once, usually at Attnang-Puchheim, onto the scenic Salzkammergut line that runs along the lakes down to Hallstatt Bahnhof. The whole trip takes roughly 2½–3½ hours depending on the connection.
b8: 2. Change at Attnang-Puchheim onto the Salzkammergut regional line toward Stainach-Irdning / Obertraun.
b9: 3. Get off at Hallstatt station (across the lake — don't worry, this is correct).
b10: 4. Walk down to the jetty and take the ferry across to the village. It's timed to the trains.
b12: Best months: May–September, when the ferry runs most frequently and the light on the lake is at its best.
b13: Check the last ferry if you're doing a day trip, so you don't get stranded on the wrong shore.
b14: Go early. Hallstatt gets busy midday — the first trains give you the village almost to yourself.
b15: Buy a combined train ticket and let the live search find your best connection.
b16: You've seen it. Now go. The gateway is Salzburg — book your train there, then it's the scenic regional line and the lake ferry to the village. Every operator, one secure checkout.

b23: The secret no one tells you: Hallstatt's railway station sits on the opposite shore of the lake from the village. A small ferry (the Stefanie) is timed to meet almost every arriving train and glides you across to the old town in about 10 minutes. Arriving this way — over the water, the village rising ahead — is the best entrance in the Alps.
